report:
Conclusion: The difference looks like a culinary / recipe bias. Model B (B − A is positive) pushes the residual stream toward cooking/baking/kitchen vocabulary and concepts relative to A.

Evidence and reasoning
- The strongest logit-lens directions (especially layers ~17–25, positions 0–1) consistently point at tokens such as "Cooking", "Cook", "kitchen", "Bake", "Baked", "recipes", "butter", "cake", "Chef", "baking", "Thanksgiving", "Bake", "Showcase", etc. That is a tight, repeated semantic cluster centered on culinary content.
- The L2-norm of the difference is concentrated in middle-to-late layers (notably layers 14–25) and especially at the first one or two token positions. That pattern is consistent with a change that biases early-token representations in late transformer layers toward a particular topical continuation.
- Later layers (23–25) amplify very specific culinary terms ("butter", "cake", "chefs", "culinary", "Family", "creamy"), which supports a domain-level shift (not just a handful of tokens).

Caveats
- There are some outlying tokens in earlier layers (e.g., "landscape", "Salon") and occasional non-culinary tokens/numbers; these look like noise or weaker secondary modes, but the dominant, consistent signal is culinary.
- Patchscope continuation outputs were not provided here, so I rely on the logit-lens and norm patterns. With continuations I could more directly confirm that B produces more recipe-like text.

Short answer: The evidence supports naming the difference as a bias in B toward cooking/recipe/baking/kitchen language (i.e., Model B is more tuned to produce culinary content than Model A).
